endorsements.quote: AI tools may serve as supplemental aids when professional interpreters are unavailable, but their deployment must be governed by enforceable standards for accuracy, transparency, and privacy.

unlisted_practices: Do not use AI-mediated interpreting as a routine replacement for qualified professional interpreters in clinical care.
Use AI interpreting tools only as optional, carefully evaluated supplements supervised by trained clinicians and professional interpreters.
Restrict AI interpreting to limited low-risk uses, such as translation of standardized materials or constrained use in high-resource languages, when professional interpreters are unavailable.

Regulators and accrediting bodies should set minimum certification standards and require independent auditing of AI interpreting tools, particularly for high-stakes clinical and consent-related encounters.
Technology vendors should be transparent about model limitations, data handling, and intended use of AI interpreting tools.
Establish community oversight of AI-mediated interpreting as part of regulatory guardrails.
Frame AI-mediated interpreting as a patient safety issue rather than solely a cost-saving tool.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint article addressing the ethical risks, structural implications, and governance/guardrail recommendations for AI-mediated medical interpreting.
